solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One of our Test opponents, unfortunately, is a natural

indicators.note: something gone unfortunately has gone wrong, so these letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A cricket fan grumbles that a rival Test side happens to be naturally gifted.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is an international cricket match; from a British setter's view, Australia is the classic opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: Australia plays Test cricket against England, so a member of its team is a typical Test opponent.

clue.text: Positions on course airline set up, making rapid descent

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the letters are read upwards, back to front

parts.note: on a golf course a ball's position is its lie, so positions are lies
BA is British Airways

explanation.surface: Someone sorts out flight positions and then drops quickly, like a plane descending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' reverses LIES plus BA as one block, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An abseil is a quick descent of a cliff or wall by sliding down a fixed rope.

clue.text: Suppress activity in court

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to crush or quash
second meaning: the racket sport played in a walled court

explanation.walkthrough: The court sounds legal, where things get suppressed, but it is a sports court.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to crush a revolt, and the noun is the racket game played indoors against walls.

clue.text: Is bloke imprisoned by Commies located again?

indicators.note: being imprisoned by means sitting inside the communists

parts.note: Commies are communists, Reds; two of them, RED and RED
cove is old British slang for a bloke

explanation.surface: A man held by communists has been tracked down once more.
explanation.walkthrough: Cove is dated British slang for a man; the plural 'Commies' is why two Reds wrap around him.
explanation.definitionFit: To find something again after it was lost is to locate it a second time.

clue.text: Choice of numbers of Romans as ruler

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for 50
OR is the word offering a choice
D is the Roman numeral for 500, a second number of the Romans

explanation.surface: Picking between Roman figures makes someone a ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Choice of numbers of Romans' as L OR D: a choice between two Roman numerals, 50 or 500.
explanation.definitionFit: A lord is a nobleman or master, one who rules over others.

clue.text: He was barely able to announce his discovery

definitions.text: He was barely able to announce his discovery

parts.words: He was barely able to announce his discovery
parts.note: the Greek mathematician famously leapt from his bath and ran naked crying Eureka

explanation.walkthrough: 'barely able' looks like 'hardly able', but it means naked: he ran out of his bath unclothed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek scientist discovered the principle of displacement in his bath and ran through the streets without clothes.

clue.text: Hostile takeover firm mounted

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
something mounted is up

explanation.surface: A business has climbed into position for an aggressive buyout.
explanation.definitionFit: A coup is a sudden seizure of power, a forcible takeover of government.

clue.text: Finished on poor horse last in race — past its best

parts.note: something finished is over
a rip is a worthless old horse

indicators.note: last in means take only the final letter of the word race

explanation.surface: A tired old nag finishes the race well past its prime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last in' takes E, the final letter of race; RIP is an old word for a worn-out horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit gone overripe has passed its peak of ripeness and is starting to spoil.

clue.text: Antiquated weapons of European alliances

parts.note: a Pole is a person from Poland
axes, as in the Axis powers, are alliances between states

explanation.surface: Old-fashioned arms belonging to the alliances of Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: A poleaxe is a medieval battleaxe on a long shaft, a weapon long out of use.

clue.text: Sensible course to follow in cinema, we hear

indicators.note: the course comes to follow the sensible word, so it is placed after it

parts.note: sound means sensible, as in sound advice
a track is a course

explanation.surface: Advice on a sensible route through the plot of a film.
explanation.definitionFit: The recorded music and dialogue accompanying a film is what the audience listens to.

clue.text: Went down hill

definitions.meaning: first meaning: dropped, past tense of fall
second meaning: a mountain or moor in northern England

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as walking down a hill, but those are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the past tense of fall and also a northern English name for an upland peak.

clue.text: Problem for runner? Trainer's got it covered

definitions.text: Problem for runner? Trainer's got it covered

parts.words: Problem for runner? Trainer's got it covered
parts.note: a fungal infection of the feet, hidden inside a sports shoe, or trainer

explanation.walkthrough: A trainer sounds like a coach who has a problem in hand, but it is a running shoe, which covers the infected foot.
explanation.definitionFit: The fungal infection between the toes is common among runners and stays hidden in sports shoes.

clue.text: Demand part for twin sister

indicators.note: the answer is only part of the words that follow, sitting within them

explanation.surface: Someone requests a role for their twin sister.
explanation.definitionFit: To insist is to demand firmly, refusing to accept a no.

clue.text: State carriage

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a state of Australia
second meaning: a light four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a state coach at a ceremony; really an Australian state and a horse-drawn carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs to an Australian state and to a low open carriage for two passengers.

clue.text: Involved in running, a miler somehow concealing a worry

indicators.note: concealing means the rearranged letters hide the other part inside them
the miler's letters are put together somehow, in a different order

parts.note: to nag is to worry at someone

explanation.surface: A middle-distance runner, involved in a race, hides an anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram turns A MILER into MERIAL; 'concealing' puts A NAG inside it after the M.
explanation.definitionFit: Managerial work concerns running an organisation, the business of managers.

clue.text: Astronomical phenomenon — top celestial arrangement

indicators.note: an arrangement of letters puts them into a new order

explanation.surface: A spectacular sight in the heavens, the finest celestial display of all.
explanation.definitionFit: When the Moon fully covers the Sun, the sky darkens: an event studied by astronomers.

clue.text: Five to nine, for example? Right

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in poker, a run of five consecutive cards such as five through nine

explanation.walkthrough: 'Five to nine' looks like a time of day, 8:55; it is a run of poker cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A poker hand of five cards in sequence has this name, and the word also means honest or correct.

clue.text: Secures what worker needs to make pub furniture

parts.note: to bar a door is to secure it
a worker needs a tool

explanation.surface: Someone fixes what a tradesman needs in order to build fittings for a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall seat at a pub counter is where drinkers perch.

clue.text: Are their customers more broad-minded?

parts.note: read broad-minded as abroad-minded: these business people serve clients with their minds on going abroad

explanation.walkthrough: Broad-minded suggests tolerance, but the pun is abroad-minded, thinking of holidays overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Firms booking holidays serve customers planning trips abroad.

clue.text: Long-distance partnership

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an old unit of distance, about three miles

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a long-distance relationship, but the old measure is about three miles.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an old measure of roughly three miles and also an alliance of parties.

clue.text: North of border, a northern part of Ireland

indicators.note: in a down clue, being north of something puts it above, so A and N come before the border

parts.note: a trim is a decorative border

explanation.surface: A region of Northern Ireland lies north of the Irish border.
explanation.definitionFit: This county lies in the north-east of Northern Ireland, on the island of Ireland.

clue.text: Within plans we're drafting, set out solution

indicators.note: within means the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: While drafting plans, someone sets out a solution to a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: To have answered something is to have given the solution to it.

clue.text: Like seabird following in wake

parts.note: as means like
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A gull trails behind a ship in its wake.
explanation.definitionFit: Astern means behind a ship, where its wake lies.

clue.text: A piece knocked off counter

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a small fragment broken away

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like something knocked off a shop counter; the counter is a casino token.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a fragment broken from a surface and also a token used in gambling.

clue.text: Fail to stop thug

explanation.walkthrough: Read as GO ON it means carry on; as one word it is a thug.
explanation.definitionFit: Two words means continue, while the single word is a hired hooligan.

clue.text: Sole provider of amount of liquor fool's swallowed

indicators.note: the measure has swallowed the fool, holding him inside

parts.note: a finger is a measure of spirits, the width of a finger in a glass
a shmo is a fool; the 's stands for has

explanation.surface: The only supplier of a dram has a fool who drank it.
explanation.definitionFit: A fishmonger sells sole and other fish, so he supplies it.

clue.text: Signalled disaster audibly had an effect

indicators.note: audibly means the word is heard, so a word of the same sound is entered

parts.note: a bell tolled to signal a death or disaster

explanation.surface: A warning of catastrophe was heard and it made its mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Strain that told on someone had a noticeable effect on them.

clue.text: Closely follow error by group of students

parts.note: a slip is an error
a stream is a group of pupils of similar ability in British schools

explanation.surface: A student gets a mistake by copying someone in class too closely.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools, pupils are divided by ability into streams.
explanation.definitionFit: To slipstream is to travel just behind another vehicle in its wake.
